description:

Plan-named follow-ups
- Ledger directories under TEST_DESIGN_STATE_DIR (or the user cache dir) are never pruned; a stale ledger for an old run ID is never consulted, but nothing removes it.
- prepare-live's own live-attempt document on live-profile-unavailable is not recorded in the ledger (record-attempt layer 3 is).
- evaluate-mutation does not run RestoreAll between sites, so untracked residue left by one site's target run makes the next site's PoliceDiff refuse ErrMultiSite; the SC-24 harness removes the residue itself. Worth running RestoreAll between sites now that it exists.

internal/runstate hygiene
- validateRunID duplicates internal/worktree/rundir.go:35-49 verbatim; lift when a third caller appears.
- lock.go: `err != syscall.EINTR` should be errors.Is.
- checkpoint_test.go: the temp-name prefix check is unreachable after the file-count check.
- No test pins that repeat over a started record still yields detail "restarted".
- saveLedger drops os.Remove cleanup errors (best effort, accepted).
- RFC3339 second granularity: Seq is the ordering authority; resume must never sort by timestamp.
- ledger.go discriminates load vs save failures by runstate's error-text prefix; a lock failure inside Load surfaces as ledger-write-failed on a read path. Typed ErrLoad/ErrSave would fix both.
- ledgerIdentity falls back to the unresolved root when EvalSymlinks fails (unreachable today because openLedger fails first).

resume.go shape
- state-unreadable overwrites an existing reason (unreachable today).
- pendingObligations takes resumeOutput by value.
- counts.invalid undercounts an inputs-unreadable review group relative to review.groups[].reason.

Ledger gate duplication and function size
- The started/completed mutation-row gate is written three times (evaluatemutation.go, recovermutation.go, preparemutation.go); lift requireStartedMutationRow into ledger.go.
- evaluateMutationOp is ~250 lines; extract the ledger gate and completeMutationRow.
- executeLiveOp gained a ~35-line ledger preamble; extract openLiveAttempt.
- recordattempt.go: the refused-attempt mutation-row inputs carry no identity or worktreePath (deliberate); add a comment.

Robustness gaps with no observed failure
- recover-mutation's recreate branch does not run RestoreAll to prove the fresh worktree (inferred from Create).
- RestoreAll compares the commit argument as a literal string; document that it must be a resolved SHA.
- mutation.LoadState does not validate Started (empty site or phase accepted).
- No test asserts the "(git clean: ...)" suffix in the ErrResidue detail.
- executelive.go: `r.cleanupFailed = failed` overwrites instead of accumulating (safe only because of the early return on failed recovery).
- runCleanupCommands drops a redaction-withheld recovery step from steps while its predicates still decide failed.
- The started-prev recover branch of execute-live is proven only by SC-23.
- No test reads the live-attempt record's inputs (planSha256) back.
- recover-mutation on a row with no marker restores a healthy workspace silently (documented; a not-interrupted refusal would be stricter).

Test-harness ergonomics
- waitForPath's timeout path never prints the helper's stderr, so a refused execute-live shows as an opaque 60 s timeout.
- waitForNoProcessMatching's timeout leaves the stalled check unkilled (it exits on its own within 20 s).
- restart_test.go: the firstCleanup > secondDeploy comparison is unreachable after the DeepEqual fatal.

title: Lazy critic can beat the single canary (N-1)/N of the time
description:
Layer 2 voids a batch when its canary verdicts HOLDS. A critic that verdicts one arbitrary row WEAK and stamps the rest HOLDS hits the canary only 1/N of the time, so the lazy strategy succeeds (N-1)/N. The sacrificed healthy row's WEAK is blocking, so the failure mode is a spurious BLOCKED on a clean branch rather than a false PASS -- but the guard is still weak.

Wording in agents/coverage-critic.md was softened so the rule is not stated in gameable form, but the math is unchanged. Inherent to one canary per batch.

Options: more than one canary per batch; or a canary whose correct verdict is known to be HOLDS as well as ones known WEAK, so no single-sacrifice strategy is safe.

Found by adversarial review 2026-08-01.
